components.name: Seasonal-Trend Decomposition via Moving Average Kernel
components.description: Decompose each input variate's raw sequence into a trend component using a moving average kernel and a seasonal component as the remainder (original minus trend).
components.quote: It first decomposes a raw data input into a trend component by a moving average kernel and a remainder (seasonal) component.

components.name: Two Independent One-Layer Linear Layers
components.description: Apply a separate linear layer (weight matrix W ∈ ℝ^{T×L}) to the trend component and another to the seasonal component, sharing weights across variates.
components.quote: Then, two one-layer linear layers are applied to each component, and we sum up the two features to get the final prediction.

components.name: Summation of Component Predictions
components.description: Add the outputs of the two linear layers (trend and seasonal) element-wise to produce the final forecast.
components.quote: Then, two one-layer linear layers are applied to each component, and we sum up the two features to get the final prediction.

components.name: Shared Weights Across Variates (No Spatial Modeling)
components.description: Use the same linear-layer weights for all variates; do not model cross-variate (spatial) correlations.
components.quote: Note that LTSF-Linear shares weights across different variates and does not model any spatial correlations.

components.name: Moving-Average-Kernel 25
components.description: The moving average used for the decomposition has kernel size 25.
components.quote: For DLinear , the moving average kernel size for decomposition is 25,
